problem: Existing trajectory-driven or reactive embodied navigation agents (MapGPT, WMNav, World-In-World) keep scene- or trajectory-level memory and fail to turn past interactions into reusable, transferable decision strategies ('experiential amnesia').
motivation: Humans improve through interaction, reflection, abstraction and adaptation; embodied agents should likewise convert experience into portable heuristics that generalize to unseen environments rather than merely replaying episodic traces. Prior self-improving agents (Reflexion, ExpeL) are mostly text/code-centric, not closed-loop multimodal embodied.
key_idea: Couple short-horizon Imagine-then-Verify planning (world model + VLM evaluator) with dual-grain memory (short-term reflective, long-term principle) and an Autonomous Knowledge Induction module that distills multimodal trajectories into a natural-language Navigation Heuristic Library fed back into planning.
insight: Ablations show SRM gives immediate within-episode gains (IGNav SR 36.11→40.18 in round 1) while LPM only helps as experience accumulates (stronger by round 3). Heuristics induced on a seen split transfer to unseen episodes (IGNav SR 34.72→48.61, SPL 24.03→39.33) and beat manually written heuristics; online updating on limited unseen episodes can overwrite good transferred priors, revealing a trade-off between fast transfer and long-term adaptation (on-split updating reaches 55.56 SR by round 5).
method: Imagine-then-Verify loop: planner proposes N candidate plans (actions + reasoning); a subtask distributor aligns actions with rationale; a world model (Wan2.1 I2V) rolls out short future observations; a VLM evaluator scores them against the goal and argmax is executed, with frequent replanning.
Memory graph: root/trajectory/subtask nodes with hierarchical and temporal edges, shared by memory modules.
Short-term Reflective Memory (SRM): a sliding window of recent subtasks is summarized by an analyzer into local progress/failure patterns and appended to the planner context within the episode.

Long-term Principle Memory (LPM): after each episode, downstream subtask trajectories are converted into guiding (success) or cautionary (failure) principles; retrieved by goal-conditioned state-embedding nearest neighbour with a threshold.
Memory consolidation: goal-wise, keeps shortest successful episodes as templates, else diverse failures.

Autonomous Knowledge Induction (AKI): a VLM heuristic extractor produces heuristics h=(pattern id, description, strategy, confidence, success/failure); clustered by pattern/semantic similarity and merged by an LLM merger into a Navigation Heuristic Library; high-confidence heuristics are fed to SRM and the planner.
Static vs adaptive: Robo-Cortex fixes memory/heuristics before testing; Robo-Cortex++ keeps updating heuristics online during inference.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct-AWQ (frozen, shared for planning, memory analysis, AKI) + Wan2.1-I2V-A14B-480P world model (frozen)
setting.training_data: none (training-free; heuristics/memory accumulated from experience episodes)
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: forward 0.20 m, turn left/right 22.5°
setting.simulator: Habitat-sim (HM3D val for IGNav/AEQA, MP3D for AR); real robot preliminary

numbers.eval_set_note: unseen half of the evaluation set, heuristics transferred from the seen half
numbers.extra: heuristics induced on seen split, no LPM, no update
numbers.evidence: Table 3 heuristic transfer study on the unseen split

numbers_note: Benchmarks are World-In-World's IGNav/AR/AEQA tasks (not canonical names); split labeled 'val' as the paper gives no official split names. Round-wise curves in a figure; some values quoted in text (e.g., on-split heuristics reach 55.56 SR / 46.29 SPL at round 5).
results: Static Robo-Cortex beats the strongest baseline World-In-World on IGNav (+2.69 SR, +4.16 SPL: 41.26/31.66 vs 38.57/27.50) and AR SR (22.39 vs 20.68); AEQA SPL is lower than WMNav (21.40 vs 23.60). Robo-Cortex++ reaches 45.07 SR / 35.06 SPL on IGNav and the best AEQA score/SPL; heuristic transfer to unseen episodes gives up to +15.30 SPL over the basic pipeline.
limitations: Real-world validation is preliminary (two indoor scenes, 4/10 goals for the basic pipeline) and small-scale.
Only one VLM (Qwen2.5-VL-72B) and one world model evaluated; model-agnosticism untested.
Online updating on few unseen episodes can overwrite useful transferred heuristics, and static AEQA SPL trails WMNav.
